title: AGNTCon + MCPCon 2026: Agentic AI Foundation Adds Four Projects as MCP Turns to Security
gist: At AGNTCon + MCPCon 2026 the Agentic AI Foundation grew to 10 projects, with new contributions from Alibaba, OpenAI, Anthropic and Hugging Face. Talks moved from protocol features to security and identity, as MCP SDK downloads hit 4.17B and Dawn Song warned that frontier AI favours attackers. The talks also flagged code review, agent identity and missing economic mechanisms as the next bottlenecks.

insights.claim: The Agentic AI Foundation went from three founding projects to ten in its first year, adding Alibaba's OpenSandbox, OpenAI's Open Responses, Anthropic's Agent Skills and Hugging Face's OpenEnv.
insights.so_what: Big AI labs are standardising agent plumbing in a neutral foundation, which commoditises the interop layer.
insights.quote: A year ago, AAIF launched with three projects and a bet that agentic AI needed a neutral home to thrive. Today we host 10.
insights.speaker: Manik Surtani

insights.claim: A license alone does not keep infrastructure open. Android stayed under one company, while Kubernetes became a shared standard after Google moved it into a neutral foundation.
insights.speaker: Manik Surtani
insights.so_what: Governance structure, not licensing, decides whether agent standards become vendor-controlled moats.

insights.claim: OpenAI's Open Responses spec is backed by AWS Bedrock, Databricks, Ollama, Nvidia and vLLM, but Anthropic still uses its own Messages API and Google its Interactions API, so the LLM interface layer is still fragmented.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: The leading model vendors still resist interface lock-in, so switching costs between model APIs persist.

insights.claim: The Register framed the AAIF as a friendly, funded foundation adopting vendor-affiliated technology, and cautioned that the rush to embrace AI agents may be too fast for some industries.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Skeptics see vendor capture behind the neutrality story, a risk if adoption runs ahead of regulated industries.
insights.quote: This enthusiastic (or credulous) embrace of AI agents may be a bit too rapid for some industries.

insights.claim: Cumulative MCP SDK downloads reached 4.17 billion, up from about 3 billion a month earlier, which maintainers say raises the stakes of every security gap.
insights.speaker: Den Delimarsky
insights.so_what: Adoption is growing about 39% month over month, so MCP is becoming core infrastructure and its attack surface is growing with it.

insights.claim: Capable models now need connectivity more than help staying on task. Stateless servers, added in the July 28 MCP spec, already carry about 70% of traffic on some platforms.
insights.speaker: David Soria Parra
insights.so_what: The value is moving from orchestration scaffolding to connectors and integrations.
insights.locator: David Soria Parra, co-creator of MCP

insights.claim: MCP tasks support in Claude Code lets tool calls run for minutes, hours or days instead of seconds, enabling long-running agent work.
insights.speaker: David Soria Parra
insights.so_what: Long-horizon agent jobs mean more compute per task and new orchestration needs.
insights.locator: David Soria Parra, co-creator of MCP

insights.claim: In ChatGPT's plugin directory, about three in four MCP tool schemas are under 1 kB, the largest reach about 260 kB for one tool and 1.4 MB for a server, and only 56% of plugins use server instructions.
insights.speaker: Thomas Sarlandie
insights.so_what: Rare production data on how MCP servers are actually built, showing context-budget pressure on tool design.

insights.claim: OpenAI rejects submitted MCP servers unless every tool carries annotations, which let ChatGPT fast-track read-only calls and ask for confirmation on destructive ones.
insights.speaker: Thomas Sarlandie
insights.so_what: Distribution platforms are setting de facto safety standards for agent tools.

insights.claim: Chrome's WebMCP, a proposed web standard now in origin trial, lets websites declare tools for agents instead of having them scrape the DOM; cited benchmarks show actions 2.5 to 7.5 times faster, and hints help resist prompt injection.
insights.speaker: Sarah Drasner
insights.so_what: An agent-readable web would reshape SEO, scraping businesses and how sites get monetised.

insights.claim: Frontier AI will help attackers more than defenders in the near term, because attackers need only one hole and models now find zero-days.
insights.speaker: Dawn Song
insights.so_what: Points to growing demand for cybersecurity and for secure-by-construction tooling.
insights.locator: Dawn Song, a UC Berkeley professor

insights.claim: On ExploitGym, GPT-5.6 Sol produced about 230 working exploits against 869 targets in two hours, and still more than 80 with standard security mitigations enabled.
insights.speaker: Dawn Song
insights.so_what: Automated exploitation is now cheap and fast, which shortens patch windows.
insights.locator: Dawn Song, a UC Berkeley professor

insights.claim: About a third of MCP's 116 conformance scenarios now test security. Enterprise-managed authorization is live in Claude, and proof-of-possession tokens and workload identity federation are in draft.
insights.speaker: Den Delimarsky
insights.so_what: Agent identity and authorization is becoming a market for identity vendors.

insights.claim: Coding agents have made code review the bottleneck: teams using them produce about 57 pull requests a week, against about 10 for other teams.
insights.speaker: Thomas Dohmke
insights.so_what: Value is moving to review, verification and intent-tracking tools, with agent session logs stored in Git and linked to commits.

insights.claim: Block's Buzz workspace gives each agent its own identity plus an attestation naming its owner. It has 80,000 communities and 36,000 GitHub stars, with version 1.0 due in mid-November.
insights.speaker: Bradley Axen
insights.so_what: Treating agents as first-class identities is turning into a product pattern.
insights.locator: Block's Bradley Axen, creator of goose

insights.claim: The AI economy lacks the mechanisms the web eventually got, such as pay-per-click advertising and secure payments. The fix is mechanism design that moves trust out of the model and into protocols, gateways and verifiable identity.
insights.speaker: Tim O'Reilly
insights.so_what: Agent payments and monetisation rails are an open opportunity.

insights.claim: AI cost should be measured per task, or better per outcome, not per token, and ultimately by business value.
insights.speaker: J.R. Storment
insights.so_what: Moving to outcome-based metrics changes how AI vendors price and how buyers judge ROI.
